# Exactness of a local law derived from history summaries

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

For a prefix-closed language L and summary q, the local law constructed from admitted one-step extensions preserves all finite continuations at every admitted history exactly iff histories sharing a code have identical continuation profiles.

Canonical source: [Readout.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Readout.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- Arbitrary event and summary types, a prefix-closed language L, and a total summary q. No finiteness, decidability or empty-word membership is required.
- The equivalence quantifies every admitted history; exactness from only one initial code is a different contract.

Histories and summaries describe one unfolding; actual admissibility and the event articulation remain supplied. Construction neither creates actual possibilities nor proves that every process has this finite-word representation.

<a id="检验与边界-validation-and-boundaries"></a>
## Validation and boundaries

Actually compiled with Lean 4.29.1: 6 new theorems and 5 definitions, 11 new empty audits plus 43 inherited empty audits. The first control-summary compilation introduced propext; explicit constructor cases removed it, with the failed record retained. Author counterreview, no independent acceptance.

Finite existential word feasibility only: no endpoint, branch-identity, probability or policy guarantee. An empty L permits vacuous validity without occurrence; the universal assumption-free foundation remains unproved.

- Admitting all Boolean words and coding only [false] as true preserves all continuations but can misrepresent encoded endpoints; merging distinct profiles produces a witnessed false continuation. [DerivedHistoryLaw.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/deeper/DerivedHistoryLaw.lean)
